basis: Inherited polyglucosan storage myopathy; skeletal muscle is affected. Immunodeficiency and cardiomyopathy vary by subtype and are not established across the group.
Defined by peripheral or autonomic nerve damage from diabetes; diabetes itself is a separate underlying disease.
Carcinoma confined to the tracheal mucosal epithelium; the trachea belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Acquired cerebral cleft malformation affecting brain structure.
Historical hereditary lipoprotein classification with no definition or phenotype supplied; metabolic assignment is provisional, with no established additional organ damage.
Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; lasting distal muscle atrophy and structural foot deformities occur in 30-79%. Restrictive ventilatory defects are <30%.
Chorioretinal degeneration and choriocapillaris atrophy are confined to the eye; broad neurovascular ancestry adds no other organ.
Inherited skeletal disorder with generalized metaphyseal enchondromas.
Cataract and glaucoma affect the eye; other reported findings are also ocular.
Severe structural skeletal myopathy. Respiratory failure and dysphagia reflect muscle weakness; intrinsic pulmonary hypoplasia and cardiomyopathy are <30%.
Closed spinal dysraphism with a spinal cord cystic malformation above the conus.
Localized benign vascular neoplasm arising in the breast; breast has no axis, and no additional organ involvement is established.
Congenital postaxial extra digit, a structural limb malformation.
Intestinal microvillus disease and retinal dystrophy define the syndrome; global developmental delay occurs in 3/10 (30%). Respiratory disease occurs in 1/10.
Malignant adipocytic soft tissue sarcoma, generally arising in deep mesenchymal tissues; no additional organ involvement is established.
Inherited macular and chorioretinal degeneration causing progressive visual loss.
Severe forebrain malformation; ocular malformations are frequent (80-99% annotated), and hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction/diabetes insipidus is common (~70% in classic HPE).
Developmental disability, cardiac defects (~33%) and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; nail aplasia is annotated in 30-79%. Tumor predisposition is a risk.
Developmental and speech delay are common across 20p deletion phenotypes; hepatic and cardiac abnormalities depend on the deleted segment and Alagille subtype.
Clonal myeloid proliferation involving blood, marrow and often spleen. Other tissue damage is variable without a supported >=30% frequency; cardiomyopathy is rare.
Severe bone fragility, osteopenia and recurrent fractures define OI8. Developmental delay in 1/2 does not establish direct CNS damage rather than skeletal motor limitation.
Glomerular sclerosis directly damages kidneys; this umbrella includes genetic, adaptive and secondary causes, so an immune mechanism is not universal.
Skeletal dysplasia and hearing loss define disease; urinary obstruction/hydronephrosis and subglottic stenosis each occur in 30-79%. Cardiac anomalies (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Bilateral congenital rudimentary postaxial extra digits constitute a structural limb malformation.
Methionine metabolism disorder; lens dislocation, skeletal disease and neurodevelopmental impairment are common (~50-80% in predominant CBS disease). Vascular disease omitted by cap.
